extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and general readers seeking an overview of German and Austrian utility models (Gebrauchsmuster)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the legal characteristics, procedural differences, and scope of protection of the German and Austrian utility model (Gebrauchsmuster), contrasting them with patents (e.g., subject-matter limits, term, prior art rules, examination, and publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter limitation: products only (Germany)
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and methods cannot be protected by a Gebrauchsmuster, only products can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes the German Gebrauchsmuster from patents; the German utility model protects product-type inventions but excludes process/method claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum term: 10 years from registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a Gebrauchsmuster, that is its maximum lifetime, is 10 years from the date of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with patents, which usually have a term of 20 years from the date of filing of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art scope: oral disclosures excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral disclosures are not taken into account for examining novelty and inventive step; only written disclosures are taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrows the prior art base relative to patent practice where oral disclosures may be relevant in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art scope: public prior use outside Germany excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Public prior use outside Germany is not taken into account when examining novelty and inventive step for the German utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior public use limited to within Germany reduces the pool of prior art compared to patents which consider wider territorial disclosures as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month grace period for applicant disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A six-month grace period before the priority date is provided for written disclosures or prior public use made by applicants or their predecessors in title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-originated disclosures within six months before priority are disregarded as prior art, offering a limited self-disclosure grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substantive examination; registration sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: They are not substantially examined. Only registration is sufficient to obtain a utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike patents where substantive examination of novelty/inventive step occurs, the German Gebrauchsmuster is granted via registration; this affects enforceability and validity assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability: made available at date of entry (Eintragungstag)
rubrics_metrics.description: German utility models are made available to the public directly when they are registered (Eintragungstag), i.e. before the publication date (Bekanntmachung).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Eintragungstag corresponds to the date a list is laid open for inspection at the DPMA premises; members of the public may inspect files from that list as of that date. By contrast, patents are made public 18 months after filing unless early publication is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing statutes and regulations (Germany)
rubrics_metrics.description: The German Gebrauchsmuster is regulated by the German Gebrauchsmuster Act (Gebrauchsmustergesetz) and the German Gebrauchsmuster Regulation (Verordnung zur Ausführung des Gebrauchsmustergesetzes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory and regulatory sources that define formal requirements, procedures, and available remedies for the German utility model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian search report timing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: In Austria, a search report is carried out within 6 to 8 months. No additional searching fee is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural step differs from Germany, where utility models are not substantially examined; Austria provides a search report as part of its procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Austrian scope of protection: broader than Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: The range of protection is broader than the German utility model. There is additional protection for: logic/algorithm for computer software; processes; therapy methods for animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking protection for software-related subject matter, processes, or veterinary therapy methods may find broader eligibility under the Austrian utility model compared to the German regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative publication timing for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are made available to the public 18 months after the filing date, unless the applicant requests early publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing is cited to contrast patent publication with the immediate public availability of German utility models at registration.
